newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end choppy day modestly lower.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end choppy day modestly lower.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed modestly lower on Thursday after a day of choppy trading, with profit-taking alternating with bargain-hunting and index futures related buying, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index fell 36.06 points, or 0.24 percent, to end at 14,795.52 after moving between 14,709.03 and 14,914.28. Turnover was HK$22.55 billion against Wednesday's HK$19.87 billion.
"Turnover is very big, the index is fairly flat," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings. "Most of the market's interest is focused on red chips."
China Everbright-IHD was very strong while utilities and properties were quiet, Osborn said.
Most-traded China Everbright-IHD hit an intra-day record high of HK$18.60 before retreating to close at HK$17.60, up HK$5.70, following an announcement on its planned acquisitions.
Sentiment was a bit cautious after index futures-linked buying erased an initial 122-point loss and added as much as 82 points to the blue-chip index, brokers said.
"The market turned choppy at the high price level," said Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research. "It's not surprised to see a retreat after the recent rally."
Hongkong Electric eased HK$0.60 to HK$28.65, Cheung Kong slipped HK$0.50 to HK$79.00 and Hutchison Whampoa was down HK$1.50 to HK$63.25.
CITIC Pacific edged up HK$0.10 to HK$49.00 and China Light jumped HK$1.10 to HK$44.20 on optimism over its developments in China and local property profits.
Brokers said the market was dominated by factors linked to Hong Kong's handover to China on July 1, with U.S. economic data due on Friday not likely to have a big effect.
"Unless the figures are very extreme either way, it's not as significant as it used to be," Osborn said.
"I still think the market will be higher next week."
Brokers said red chip companies were seen jostling for funds to buy assets from their mainland parents before the handover.
Boosted by asset injection hopes, red chips dominated the most traded list on Thursday.
The Hang Seng Chinese Enterprises Index for H-shares rose 8.72 points, or 0.81 percent, to 1,086.08.
Jingwei Textile led the rise, adding HK$0.13, or 10.24 percent, to HK$1.40.
